title: The Bullet Cluster as a Frozen-Transfer Test: Baryonic Mass Versus the S(I) Organization-Dependent Gravitational Background Response
content: Several approaches have been developed to account for the gravitational discrepancy between the dynamics inferred from observations and the gravitational effect reconstructed from the visible baryonic distribution. \(\Lambda\)CDM and MOND provide two prominent but conceptually different interpretations of this discrepancy. At galactic scales, the empirical regularities summarized by the radial acceleration relation show that the discrepancy is strongly organized by the baryonic acceleration and the characteristic scale \(a_0\). This paper asks whether acceleration alone is sufficient to organize the phenomenology across galaxies, groups, clusters, and merging clusters. Within a reconstruction-first approach, we introduce the organization-dependent response hypothesis \[ \Delta\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{rec}} = S(I)\,\Delta\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{ref}}(\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{bar}}/a_0), \qquad \Delta\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{rec}} = \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{obs}} - \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{bar}}. \] The scale \(a_0\) organizes the regime in which the reconstruction difference becomes relatively visible, while \(S(I)\) tests whether its amplitude also depends on an independently measurable property \(I\) of the baryonic structure. The central contribution is the Frozen-Transfer Protocol: \[ \text{galaxies} \to I \to S(I) \to \text{freeze} \to \text{clusters} \to \text{Bullet Cluster}. \] The definition and orientation of \(I\), the sign and functional family of \(S(I)\), its normalization, hyperparameters, control model, component rules, and primary transfer metric must be fixed using galactic training and validation data before cluster application. RAR residuals provide the primary calibration target; baryonic compactness or potential structure is the primary candidate class, with bound baryonic fraction as a secondary transfer variable. The Bullet Cluster is the terminal stress test rather than the calibration target. In \(\Lambda\)CDM, the displacement between the dominant X-ray gas and the galaxy-centred lensing structures is commonly associated with collisionless dark-matter halos. In MOND-based work, the IGIMF route instead increases the galaxy-centred baryonic mass through stellar-remnant populations. The present framework tests a third, empirically distinguishable possibility: baryonic mass dominance and organization-dependent gravitational response dominance need not coincide. The paper does not provide a completed explanation of the Bullet Cluster or a covariant lensing theory. Its falsifiable claim is narrower: if no preregistered structural variable survives galactic validation and frozen cross-system transfer, the proposed organization-dependent response program fails.
